abstract: Cubic tenfolds are the first cubic hypersurfaces for which the rational Hodge conjecture (HC) is open in the middle degree. For Thom–Sebastiani tenfolds $X=V(g(x)+h(y))\subset\mathbb P^{11}$, with $g,h$ cubic forms in six disjoint sets of variables and $T_g,T_h$ the transcendental parts of $H^4$ of the cubic fourfolds $V(g),V(h)$, we prove that HC holds for $X$ if and only if every Hodge morphism $T_g\to T_h$ is algebraic, i.e. $\mathrm{HC}(X)\iff\mathrm{HC}(V(g)\times V(h))$. The proof uses the Katsura–Shioda inductive structure $\mathrm{Bl}\,X\cong\mathrm{Bl}(X'_g\times X'_h)/\mu_3$, $X'_g=V(g+u^3)$, proved here for arbitrary $g,h$; HC for cubic fourfolds; and a level-one lemma (Paranjape–Kollár, Bloch–Srinivas) making all Hodge classes in the $\mu_3$-twisted part algebraic. Combining Beauville–Donagi with Markman's theorem on rational Hodge isometries of $K3^{[n]}$-type varieties, every Hodge isometry $T_g\cong T_h$ is algebraic, with no associated K3 surface needed. Hence HC holds for $X$ unless $T_g\cong T_h$ and the Hodge morphisms are not spanned by isometries (non-isometric rational similitudes, a norm obstruction in the CM case, or real multiplication), cases analogous to those open for $K3\times K3$. This covers very general pairs, and $g=h$ or Fourier–Mukai partners when $\mathrm{End}_{\rm Hdg}(T_g)$ is $\mathbb Q$ or CM. For pairs of triple covers $V(F+x_5^3)$, the van Geemen–Izadi Kuga–Satake correspondence makes all Hodge morphisms algebraic, so HC holds on the whole 20-dimensional family $V(F(x)+x_5^3+F'(y)+y_5^3)$. The rational-similitude case occurs over every very general cubic fourfold; it disappears when one factor has imaginary quadratic multiplication of odd dimension, e.g. $V(F+x_5^3+h)$ with $F$ very general and $h$ arbitrary. We also settle a two-dimensional family with real multiplication by $\mathbb Q(\sqrt3)$, via Varesco's theorem transported by Markman's. For every other splitting $a+b=12$ we identify the exact residue on which HC depends. The same method gives $\mathrm{HC}(V(g+h))\iff\mathrm{HC}(S_g\times S_h)$ for quartic sixfolds. Bearing on HC: new unconditional cases in the first open cubic dimension; general cubic tenfolds are not addressed.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary: v2, corrections requested in the v1 acceptance review: (1) g=h and Fourier–Mukai partners are claimed only when End(T_g) is Q or CM; the open cases are called analogous to, not identical with, the K3xK3 case. (2) Remark 6.2 rewritten: the comparison a=phi^dagger phi lies in K^+; the CM residue is a norm condition in K^+, not a rational similitude; Question 4 is the precise open statement; the Varesco remark is restricted to similarities. (3) Prop 2.1: the stratum g(x)=h(y)=0, x,y nonzero, is treated (preimage in E), giving quasi-finiteness; Theorem 5: decomposition is pt x V + Gamma. (4) t93.py includes the determinant factor zeta (ranks unchanged); README lists numpy. (5) Laterveer arXiv:1708.05278 and 1708.05671 are cited and distinguished from the new argument; numbered references with titles; LaTeX in the abstract; 522 is stated to be a complex Hodge-number count. (6) New Proposition 6.5: if End(T_g) is imaginary quadratic of odd dimension and A_g, A_h are rationally isometric, then Hom is spanned by isometries and HC holds; Corollary 6.6: such K must be Q(sqrt-3) when A=Qh^2, and HC holds for V(F+x_5^3+h) for F very general and every h. (7) New §7B (Theorem 6); the v1 discussion bullet on other splittings, which understated the residues, is replaced by it: for every splitting a+b=12 of a cubic tenfold, HC(V(g+h)) is equivalent to algebraicity of an explicit residue; the 6+6 residue is the only one of K3 type. (8) New Proposition 6.7: if T_W(-1) is Hodge isometric to T(S) for a K3 surface S, the identification is algebraic (Markman via F(W) and S^[2]), with no Fourier–Mukai equivalence assumed; Corollary 6.8 transfers Varesco's real-multiplication theorem (existence of such cubic fourfolds not checked). (9) New Corollary 6.9 with exact certificate t95c.py: a two-dimensional family of smooth cubic fourfolds with real multiplication by Q(sqrt3) (T = U^2 + A2(7)^2, root-free complement) for which HC holds for V(g+g).
title: The Hodge conjecture for Thom–Sebastiani cubic tenfolds (and quartic sixfolds)
